From: Dr. Helen Morris <hmorris@portico.edu>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Academic credits for Portico College AI Lab trial

Hi Dev,

I'm Helen, faculty lead for the AI Lab at Portico College. We're piloting a small research project this semester (faculty + 6 grad students) and would like to evaluate Redwood for inference workloads. Can you advise if there's an academic credits program we can apply for? We'd prefer self-serve credits so students can sign up and run experiments without an invoice cycle.

Attached is a short form with project details. Happy to follow any verification steps (institution email, letter of intent, etc.). Our timeline is tight — would like to start the week of Mar 15.

Thanks,
Dr. Helen Morris
Faculty, AI Lab
Portico College
Attachment: credit_request_form.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:17:00 -07:00

Hi Helen — great to connect, and thanks for the form.

Short answer: yes, we have an academic credits program that supports faculty-led research and student projects. For small pilots we can issue self-serve credits tied to institutional verification (edu email + brief LOI). I'll start the internal approval and loop in our credits team. Can you confirm the total estimated monthly token volume or a rough dollar estimate? That helps me pick an appropriate credit tier.

Next steps from our side: Marcus will confirm the tier and Laura (manager) will sign off on the allocation. If approved, we can issue credits to the domain (portico.edu) and provide a short onboarding doc for students. Expect a decision within 48 hours.

Best,
Dev Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: Academic credits for Portico College AI Lab trial

Dev — saw Helen's note and the form. Project looks like a low-risk academic trial. They requested a student-friendly self-serve approach. Proposed allocation: $3,000 in hosted credits for 3 months, domain-locked to @portico.edu with per-user caps (to avoid abuse). Includes access to standard curated models (no dedicated infra).

Two things: 1) We need a manager sign-off on the $3k promotional allocation, and 2) confirm we can enforce the domain restriction via our signup flow (engineering has a domain verification step).

If Laura approves I can create the HubSpot deal and generate the credit bundle. I attached our academic policy draft for reference.

Marcus
Principal Sales Specialist

Thanks Marcus — endorsing the $3,000 credit allocation for the pilot. A couple of guardrails:

- Make credits domain-locked to portico.edu and require sign-up with institutional email.
- Set per-account monthly burn cap at $800 to keep things within the pilot budget.
- Require a short LOI (one paragraph) from Helen confirming research scope and student access.

Marcus: please create the HubSpot record (deal PLG-2026-0427) and include the LOI as a note. Dev: you can confirm to Helen and ask for the LOI. Once LOI is received we can generate credits within 24 hours.

Laura Bennett

Hi Helen — great news: we've approved a pilot allocation. Summary and next steps below.

Allocation: $3,000 hosted credits, valid for 3 months (Mar 15 — Jun 14).
Controls: domain-locked to @portico.edu; per-account monthly cap $800.
Required: brief LOI (one paragraph) confirming faculty oversight and student list (names + portico.edu emails preferred).

What we'll do once we have the LOI:
- Create a HubSpot deal (PLG-2026-0427) and issue the credit bundle.
- Send onboarding note with signup link and instructions for students to claim credits (self-serve flow with domain verification).

Please send the LOI when convenient — if you can paste it in a reply here we can proceed immediately.

Thanks again, and excited to support the lab.

Best,
Dev Patel
